findings.problem: Nine dots each flying its own diagonal from the mark to its row read as a particle effect.
findings.fix: Rebuilt as two orthogonal legs — spread vertically into row order, then align left onto the rail; reversed on the way home. It now reads as a grid unfolding into a list and matches the film's route grammar.

findings.problem: The scan head parked on the row it had found and struck through the text for 40 frames. A reading head that stays is a decoration.
findings.fix: It leaves once Hookflo has written its marker.

findings.problem: The failing row lost its status chip when the panel contracted, right as the alert card claims 410.
findings.fix: The timestamp column still drops in the narrow panel; the chip never does, because it is the evidence.

findings.problem: 'email · slack · webhook — all channels acknowledged' was a claim rather than evidence, and the most advertising-shaped thing in the piece.

limits: No sound. The score assumes a metronome that misses a beat at the drop and a Slack knock at the alert; neither exists in the render. The drop is designed to be heard before it is seen.
The ending's meaning is thin without the setup: that the alerted marker lands on the mark's white dot is legible only to a viewer who registered the white dot in the first three seconds.
The panel stays dead-centre for four of the eight states. Deliberate — it is one persistent object being re-read — but it is the most symmetrical choice available.
